title: Dawn flip orchestra — lightweight runbook + one-liner stash
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational playbook for low-traffic "dawn" flip windows. Goal is a minimal, repeatable checklist that on-call + morning shift can run with 1–2 people and regain safety quickly if anything smells off. This is intentionally terse — keep it readable as a terminal cheat sheet.

Principles:
- Keep cohorts small at first (1–3% traffic) for tenanted customers.
- Prefer fast, observable steps over long waits. If metrics move, abort and pin.
- Use explicit tenant-sync step to avoid upstream cache-staleness induced regressions.
- Target timebox: full flip in <= 40 minutes if happy path.

Preflight (T-45 min):
- Confirm deploy image hash + manifest (PR #487) matches release tag.
- Run smoke job locally: ./scripts/smoke-dawn --model=stable-alpha --seq=64 (expected: pass in < 350ms).
- Check capacity reservations (Dedicated pools) for target region: Infra Slack/bot shows available GPUs >= planned.
- Confirm DB migrations: none scheduled. If any, move to later window.
- Create ephemeral dashboard: copy template "dawn-flip-vitals" + set cohort filter.

Quick checklist (operator steps):
1) Announce: #deploys "Dawn flip starting — tag v3.2.1-dawn — taking initial 1%". Drop pinned message with abort signal (emoji :no_entry:).
2) Enable warmup cohort (internal routing toggle) for seed tenants (IDs list in linked artifacts).
3) Push model variant to canary pool with pin-by-tenant. Command: deployctl push --tag v3.2.1-dawn --pool canary-dawn --pin tenants-file.json
4) Validate warmup traces: ensure KV cache primed (metrics: kv_miss_rate drops within 2 min).
5) Health probes: hit /health and /vitals endpoints across 3 AZs. If any 5xx or >2% error rate -> roll back.
6) Observe latency and token cost for 5 minutes. Thresholds: p95 latency < 450ms, error rate < 1%, token-cost delta < +12%.
7) If green, increase traffic to 5% across cohort buckets. Wait 10 min.
8) Check for drift/regression in quality monitors (sampled prompt set): run quick eval harness (eval-runner quick-dawn). If unknown regressions in safety filters -> abort.
9) Ramp to 25% if stable for 20 minutes.
10) Final step: release global variant and remove tenant pins. Post-note to #deploys.

Rollback triggers (immediate actions):
- Any sudden spike in error rate > 3% sustained 2 minutes -> freeze traffic, pin back to previous tag, notify SRE.
- Latency p95 > 1s for >5 minutes -> warmback to previous variant, capture heap/profile.
- Safety filter failures or customer PII redaction regressions -> immediate pin and incident channel.

One-liners for Slack / Terminal (copyable):
- Announce start: "dawn flip: starting canary v3.2.1-dawn -> 1% seed cohort. Contact @oncall if issues."
- Freeze traffic: "dawn flip: HOLD — freezing traffic and pinning to v3.2.0. Hotfix/rollback initiated."
- Abort and rollback: "dawn flip: ABORT — rolling back to v3.2.0 and notifying customers. See incident #INF-1922."
- Quick health check curl: "curl -sS https://canary.dawn.redwood/v1/health | jq .status"

Observability knobs to watch (dashboard widgets):
- p95 latency by model variant and AZ (color top red at 800ms).
- Error rate by tenant (alert if any single tenant >2%).
- KV cache hit ratio over time (should climb after warmup).
- Token-cost delta per 10k requests.
- Safety filter false-positive/false-negative counters via eval-sampler ingestion.

Tenant sync step (important):
- Run tenant-sync script to push latest prompt_templates + routing hints: ./ops/tenant-sync --tenants seed-list.json --blocking
- Verify sync logs for 0 failures. If failures, isolate tenants and proceed with smaller cohort.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should the initial ramp be 2% instead of 1% for our multi-tenant spike history? Need retrospective on last 6 dawn flips. @Nina to pull.
- Add a fast rollback script to flip traffic in <30s (we currently need manual pinning across infra).
- Consider automated canary judge (small classifier on safety signals) to block ramps — prototype in infra/auto-judge.

Postmortem template (if anything goes wrong):
- Timeline (minute granularity), who did what, metrics snapshots.
- Root cause, action items (with owners), retrospective notes for cohort sizing.

Handy command snippets (ops binder):
- Push + pin: deployctl push --tag v3.2.1-dawn --pool canary-dawn && deployctl pin --tag v3.2.1-dawn --tenants seed-list.json
- Check metrics tail: infra-metrics tail --dashboard dawn-flip-vitals --minutes 15
- Quick rollback: deployctl pin --tag v3.2.0 --selector all-active-canaries

References & links:
- Linear ticket for automation: INF-1922
- PR with deploy scripts changes: github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-scripts/pull/487
- Dash template: confluence.redwood/ops/dash-templates#dawn-flip-vitals

Shelf notes (for future editions):
- Add sample prompt set for quality checks embedded in dashboard.
- Make tenant-sync non-blocking with detailed diff output.
- Build a canned Slack workflow for announcing and aborting flips.

Final: this is intentionally brief — keep this file as the on-shift single page cheat. Expand to proper runbook once we stabilize the automation bits.

-- Riley (notes)
